items.followUp: State Newton’s third law of motion and explain it using the recoil of a gun.

rubric.why: The answer must identify the action–reaction relationship.
rubric.description: States that every action has a reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the action and reaction.

rubric.why: The action and reaction forces have equal magnitudes.
rubric.description: States that the forces are equal in magnitude.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for equality of magnitude.

rubric.why: The action and reaction forces act in opposite directions.
rubric.description: States that the forces are opposite in direction.

rubric.why: A specific example shows how the action–reaction pair operates.
rubric.description: Explains the law with the example of walking.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the action and reaction in the example.

modelAnswer: Newton’s third law states that for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.
The action and reaction forces act simultaneously on two different bodies.
When we walk, our foot pushes the ground backwards and the ground pushes us forwards.
These two forces are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.

items.followUp: A square plate has a side of 10 mm. Find the pressure exerted on it by a force of 20 N.

rubric.why: The side length must be converted to SI units before calculating the area.
rubric.description: Converts the side length to 0.020 m.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct conversion to metres.

rubric.why: The pressure calculation requires the area of the square face.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct area with unit.

rubric.why: This is the relation used to calculate pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

rubric.why: The given force and calculated area must be substituted correctly.
rubric.description: Substitutes the values into the pressure formula.

rubric.why: The result must be calculated and expressed as pressure in pascals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct numerical answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: side = 20 mm = 0.020 m; force, F = 40 N.
Area of the square, A = side² = (0.020 m)² = 4.0 × 10⁻⁴ m².
Therefore, the pressure on the pin head is 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa.
